title: Why Every Reaction Is a Choice Between Heaven and Hell (A Zen Parable)
fullTitle: Soul Snack #93: Why Every Reaction Is a Choice Between Heaven and Hell (A Zen Parable)

promo.text: Join the Seat of the Soul monthly newsletter and receive weekly, wisdom filled, insights from Gary.

description: Gary illustrates this with the story of Hakuin, a founder of Zen Buddhism, confronted by an armed samurai demanding to know if heaven and hell exist. Hakuin provoked the samurai’s fury, then calmly named the moment his sword began to leave its sheath “the gates of hell,” and the moment he sheathed it again “the gates of heaven” – showing that even ordinary moments are ongoing invitations to choose between the two.
The solution Gary offers: every interaction, however small, is a chance to choose awareness and love over fear – and intention is the key that determines which gate opens.

chapters.title: Gary opens by describing the new consciousness transforming the human species and the choice between two worlds:
chapters.text: one of gratitude and contentment, the other of anger and despair.

chapters.title: Gary explains the nature of choice as walking through doors that close behind you,
chapters.text: and names intention as the key to creating Authentic Power.

chapters.text: confronted by an armed samurai demanding to know if heaven and hell exist.

outro: (03:58) — Gary connects the story to everyday partnership moments, noting that spiritual partners help each other see this choice most clearly when a frightened part of the personality makes it hardest to see.

Think of a recent moment when you felt triggered by something small – a comment, a tone, an unmet expectation. In that instant, which gate did you walk through? Before reacting next time, pause and ask: is a frightened part of my personality making this choice for me? What would it look like to choose the gate to heaven instead?
